confirmed.title: History visit identity differs between the record and the history_visits primary key, so one record fails an entire apply batch
confirmed.failure_scenario: A PageRecord arrives whose visit set holds {at_ms:100, device:7, transition:link} and {at_ms:100, device:7, transition:typed} (a duplicated device id from a copied profile, as the design explicitly allows, or any buggy/malicious peer). PageRecord::join unions them, normalize() keeps both, store_page -> write_visits does a plain INSERT into history_visits whose PK is (url, at_ms, device), SQLite raises UNIQUE, apply_one returns Err, and SyncStore::apply rolls back the whole batch including unrelated kinds. Proven with the real crate: apply -> Err("UNIQUE constraint failed: history_visits.url, history_visits.at_ms, history_visits.device") and a good Prefs record in the same batch was lost. With the documented dumb server the record stays there forever and every download that includes it fails, blocking sync.
confirmed.evidence: history.rs:78-83 `Visit` derives Ord/Eq over (at_ms, device, transition), and the doc on line 76 claims identity is (at_ms, device); history.rs:112 `self.visits.extend(other.visits)` unions by the full triple; history.rs:137-142 normalize() never dedupes; history.rs:346-353 write_visits uses `INSERT INTO history_visits` (no OR IGNORE) after DELETE; schema.sql:62 `PRIMARY KEY (url, at_ms, device)`; sync.rs:182-185 propagates the Err out of the transaction, contradicting design/core.md 'Bad records are reported and skipped, never partly applied'. tests/convergence.rs:522-524 even generates such visit sets for lattice_laws but only in memory, never through the table.
confirmed.fix: Make the two identities agree: implement Ord/Eq for Visit on (at_ms, device) only (choose a deterministic tie rule for transition, e.g. max), or dedupe in normalize() by (at_ms, device) keeping the max transition, so every device converges to the same set and write_visits can never collide. Do not use INSERT OR IGNORE alone, since it would make the stored set depend on iteration order.

votes.reason:
I confirmed the defect from the code and reproduced it with the real vsesvit-core crate.

**How it fails**
- `Visit` derives `Eq` and `Ord` over all three fields, `(at_ms, device, transition)` (history.rs:78-83). The doc comment above it says identity is `(at_ms, device)`.
- `PageRecord::join` merges visit sets with `self.visits.extend(other.visits)` (history.rs:112). Two visits that differ only in `transition` therefore both survive.
- `normalize` (history.rs:137-142) only applies deletion directives and the cap. It never dedupes by `(at_ms, device)`.
- `write_visits` (history.rs:346-353) runs a plain `INSERT` into `history_visits`, whose primary key is `(url, at_ms, device)` (schema.sql:62). SQLite raises a UNIQUE error.
- That error is returned through `apply_one` (sync.rs:302), then `apply_typed`, then `apply_wire`, and out of the `self.p.write` closure in `SyncStore::apply` (sync.rs:180-181). The whole transaction rolls back.
- This breaks the promise in design/core.md:308 that "Bad records are reported and skipped, never partly applied." The `rejected` path only covers JSON, id and `compatible` failures.

**Reproduction** (a throwaway crate in the scratchpad that depends on the snapshot's vsesvit-core; no snapshot files were changed)
1. **Crafted record, same batch.** A good `PageRecord` for b.example was applied in the same batch as a `PageRecord` holding `{100, dev 7, Link}` and `{100, dev 7, Typed}`. `apply` returned `Err("UNIQUE constraint failed: history_visits.url, history_visits.at_ms, history_visits.device")`. Afterwards `changes_since` showed 0 stored pages, so the good record was lost too.
2. **Copied profile, no crafting.** Two profiles were opened with the same `DeviceId(7)` and the same clock. A ran `record_visit(url, Link)`; B ran `record_visit(url, Typed)`. A then applied B's exported record and got the same UNIQUE error. So legitimate code paths can produce the collision, not only a malicious peer.

**Where the scenario does not reach**
- A single device's own table cannot produce the duplicate. `record_visit` skips an existing `(at_ms, device)` (history.rs:181), and `load_visits` reads from the primary-keyed table.
- Legitimate triggers therefore need either a copied profile (design/core.md:481 admits device ids get duplicated this way) visiting the same URL in the same millisecond, or a buggy or hostile record.
- The snapshot has no production sync engine yet. The only caller outside tests is the debug-only `apply_sync_file` in vsesvit-gtk/src/app.rs:394. The claim that a dumb server would block sync forever is about a future engine; what is true today is that the core `apply` contract is violated.

**Severity: medium, not high.** The failure is real and reproduced, but the legitimate trigger is rare and no shipping sync engine uses this path yet.

The code mismatch is real, but no real user can hit it today.

What the code does:
- `Visit` derives `Ord`/`Eq` over the full triple (at_ms, device, transition) at history.rs:78-83.
- `join` unions visits at history.rs:112, and `normalize` at history.rs:137-142 never removes duplicates.
- `write_visits` at history.rs:346-353 does a plain INSERT, but the primary key at schema.sql:62 is (url, at_ms, device).
- So a record holding two visits that differ only in transition returns an error from `store_page`. That error goes through `apply_one` (sync.rs:302) and `apply_typed` (sync.rs:385) and rolls back the whole `SyncStore::apply` transaction. That breaks the rule in core.md:308 that bad records are "reported and skipped, never partly applied".

Why no real user reaches it:
1. There is no sync engine. core.md:20 says "No sync server or plugin system now." The only product caller of `sync().apply` is `apply_sync_file` in crates/vsesvit-gtk/src/app.rs:371-394. It is behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` and is a self-test hook that reads a local file, so release builds never call it. The WinUI shell has no caller at all.
2. A correct device never creates such a pair. `record_visit` (history.rs:181-183) already skips a new visit when one with the same (at_ms, device) exists. The only honest way to get the pair is a copied profile, which shares the device id. Both copies would then have to visit the same URL in the same millisecond with different transitions, which is vanishingly unlikely. The other way is a buggy or malicious peer, and there is no peer channel yet.

This is a latent problem that becomes worth fixing when a real sync engine lands: make `normalize` keep one visit per (at_ms, device), or key `Visit` identity on (at_ms, device). It is not a defect a user of the current browser can hit.

confirmed.title: Lww<Option<JsonText>> cannot represent a JSON null value on the wire: it is read back as None, so storage.sync.set({k:null}) diverges across devices and echoes forever
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Linux an extension calls chrome.storage.sync.set({k: null}); vsesvit-webext/src/bridge.rs:244-246 forwards Value::Null to ExtStorage::set, which stores Some(JsonText("null")). changes_since serializes it as {"value":{"v":null,"at":...}}. Device B applies it and gets None (a removal): B's get() shows no key while A's shows k=null. Worse, when A downloads its own upload back from the dumb server, the parsed record (None) differs from local (Some("null")), apply_one marks it dirty and re-uploads; this repeats every sync round. Proven with the real crate: peer get() is empty, and re-applying A's own upload yields pending=1 twice in a row. Same asymmetry applies to any pref whose serialized value is JSON null (Prefs::set is generic).
confirmed.evidence: crdt.rs:264-266 `#[serde(into = "serde_json::Value", from = "serde_json::Value")] struct JsonText` makes Some(JsonText("null")) serialize as a bare `null`; serde's Option<T> deserializes `null` as None, so the wire form of the LWW value field in ext_storage.rs:65 and prefs.rs:83 is lossy exactly for the null value; sync.rs:297 `dirty = merged != incoming` then fires on every re-download of the device's own record, which is the echo the design (core.md 'When merged == incoming nothing is marked, so records do not echo') rules out. tests/convergence.rs:298 and 555-557 never generate a JSON null value, so the property test cannot see it.
confirmed.fix: Give the LWW value field a serde representation that distinguishes 'no value' from 'JSON null': e.g. serialize Option<JsonText> with a helper that omits the key (or emits a distinct marker) for None and emits the JSON for Some, with the matching deserializer, and bump nothing else; alternatively store JsonText on the wire as its canonical string so `null` stays a string. As a stopgap reject Value::Null at ExtStorage::set/Prefs::set, but that still leaves the record type unable to round-trip.

votes.reason:
I confirmed this by running the real vsesvit-core. I built a throwaway probe crate in the scratchpad that depends on the snapshot by path; the snapshot itself was not modified.

**Why the null is lost**
- `JsonText` (crdt.rs:264-266) serializes through `serde_json::Value`, so `Some(JsonText("null"))` goes out as a bare `null`.
- serde reads a bare `null` for an `Option` back as `None`.
- `SyncItemRecord.value` (ext_storage.rs:65) is a `Lww<Option<JsonText>>`. So is `PrefRecord.value` (prefs.rs:83).
- The wire body is `serde_json::to_vec(&rec)` (sync.rs:417) and is read back with `serde_json::from_slice` (sync.rs:371). A record holding a JSON null therefore cannot survive the trip.

**How an extension reaches it**
- JS `storage.sync.set` is bridged directly (api.js:124).
- bridge.rs:244-246 passes the `Value::Null` untouched to `ExtStorage::set`.
- `ExtStorage::set` (ext_storage.rs:101-121) stores `Some(JsonText::from_value(Null))`.

**Probe results**
- Device A: `set({k:null})`, then `get` returns `{"k": Null}`.
- The wire body is `{"ext":..,"key":"k","value":{"v":null,"at":..}}`.
- Device B applies it with `merged=1` and `get` returns `{}`, so the two devices disagree. B also emits a spurious `StorageChange{old_value: None, new_value: None}`.
- A re-applies its own uploaded record three times. Each time the result is `unchanged=1`, but `changes_since` returns `pending=1`.
- The mechanism: `Lww::join` keeps local `Some("null")`, because at an equal stamp `None` sorts before `Some`. Then `dirty = merged != incoming` (sync.rs:296-297) is true. The row gets a fresh seq and is re-uploaded on every round.
- This is exactly the echo that sync.rs:23-24 says cannot happen ("When merged == incoming nothing is marked, so records do not echo").
- A plain serde round-trip of `Lww{v: Some(JsonText(null))}` compares unequal to the original.

**Adjustments to the claim**
- **Severity:** no sync engine exists yet (sync.rs:1 "no engine is built now"). Nobody is hit today; the promised convergence/no-echo contract and the wire format the future engine will use are what's broken. So I rate it medium, not high.
- **Prefs:** `Prefs::set` is also affected in principle. But none of the current pref types (String, SearchEngineId, Theme, Startup, TabsPosition, bool) serialize to null. In practice only `storage.sync` on Linux reaches the bug.

The serde mechanism is correct but no real user can reach it. crdt.rs:264-266 serializes JsonText through serde_json::Value, so Some(JsonText("null")) in Lww<Option<JsonText>> (ext_storage.rs:65) goes on the wire as a bare `null`. serde reads that back as None. apply_one (sync.rs:297) then computes merged(Some@t) != incoming(None@t), so a device re-downloading its own storage.sync {k:null} record would be marked dirty every round, and a peer would store it as a removal. bridge.rs:244-246 does pass Value::Null through to ExtStorage::set. Prefs are not affected in practice: none of the defined prefs (prefs.rs:64-77) serialize to null.

Reachability is the problem. sync.rs:1 says "Nothing in core calls it, and no engine is built now", and PLAN.md:114 and core.md:207 also list the sync engine as future work. No code outside tests calls changes_since. The only caller of SyncStore::apply is the #[cfg(debug_assertions)] self-test hook apply_sync_file (vsesvit-gtk/src/app.rs:370-394), which is not a user path. Locally the value is stored and read correctly: the DB column holds the text "null", which is not SQL NULL, so live() at ext_storage.rs:151 returns k=null. That means no user sees divergence, data loss or echo in the shipped browser.

It is a latent gap in the future sync wire format that the convergence test misses. It can be fixed before any engine ships without migrating stored data. It is not a defect a real user can hit today.

confirmed.title: A local XPI can take the Chrome id of a signature-verified install, replace it and inherit its storage
confirmed.failure_scenario:
1. The user has extension X, id eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb, installed from a signed CRX (the same holds for a Chrome Web Store install), with secrets in chrome.storage.local.
2. The user drops in an unsigned local .xpi whose manifest has `browser_specific_settings.gecko.id` = that 32-char Chrome id and a version of at least X's.
3. The install succeeds and core now lists X as source=XpiFile, verification=LocalXpi, name "Evil".
4. `ext_storage().get(X, Local)` returns X's stored data to the new code.
5. On Windows the verified extension is also dropped from the engine, because its row now points at the XPI dir.
6. The synced record still says X is installed from the Chrome Web Store, so reconcile never brings the verified copy back.
I reproduced this with a scratch harness against the snapshot (scratchpad/harness, scenario 1). Output: `after XPI: id=eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb source=XpiFile ... verification=LocalXpi` and `storage visible to XPI id: {"vault": "secret-data"}`.
confirmed.evidence:
- install.rs:407-419: an XPI's id is whatever `ExtensionId::parse` accepts from the manifest gecko id. That includes Chrome-style `[a-p]{32}` ids (mod.rs:71-77). For `XpiId::FromPath` nothing binds it to a key or a signature.
- mod.rs:281-313: `commit` only compares versions against the existing row. It never checks whether the existing install is key-bound (`ChromeWebStore`/`LocalCrx`) while the new one is not. It upserts the row with the new source, verification and dir.
- Storage is keyed only by the id (schema.sql:130-135 `ext_storage_local(ext, key)`), and commit does not clear it.
- Chrome ids are otherwise only reachable through a verified key: crx.rs:197-205 for CRX files and `key_id` for unpacked dirs.
confirmed.fix: In `stage` for `Format::Xpi`, reject gecko ids that are Chrome-style (`ExtensionId::is_chrome_style`). In `commit`, refuse to replace an existing row whose id is key-bound (verification `ChromeWebStore`/`LocalCrx`, or a manifest `key`) unless the staged install proves the same key.

votes.reason:
Confirmed from the code and by rebuilding and running the scratchpad harness (scenario 1) against the snapshot myself. Output: `[1] real: id=eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb verification=LocalCrx` -> `[1] after XPI: id=eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb source=XpiFile{..} verification=LocalXpi name=Evil` -> `[1] storage visible to XPI id: {"vault": String("secret-data")}`.

Code path, all in the snapshot:
- crates/vsesvit-core/src/extensions/install.rs:407-419 (`stage`, `Format::Xpi`): the id is `ExtensionId::parse(manifest.gecko_id)`; the `(Some(g), _) => g` arm applies to `XpiId::FromPath` with no key or signature binding. `ExtensionId::parse` (mod.rs:71-77) accepts any `[A-Za-z0-9._@{}-]{1,80}`, so a 32-char `[a-p]` Chrome id passes; `manifest.rs:598-600` extracts `gecko.id` with no validation. This violates the documented invariant at mod.rs:63 ("Chrome-style ... derived from a public key").
- crates/vsesvit-core/src/extensions/mod.rs:275-321 (`commit`): the only guard against an existing row is `cmp_versions(...) == Less` (l.282-289); nothing compares the existing row's `verification`/`source` against the staged one. The XPI row upserts via `INSERT OR REPLACE` (l.652-671) with `local_enabled = Some(true)` (l.301-304), which satisfies the CHECK constraint in extensions/schema.sql:28, so the replace succeeds over a `ChromeWebStore`/`LocalCrx` row.
- Storage is keyed only by id: src/schema.sql:130-135 `ext_storage_local(ext, key)`; `ext_storage.rs:148-160` `live()` selects `WHERE ext = ?1`; `commit` never clears it (only `delete_local`, l.525-529, does, and it is not called on replace). On Linux the runtime uses the core id directly: vsesvit-webext/src/extension.rs:123 `id: installed.id.clone()`, bridge.rs:236 `store.get(&ext.id, ..)`, and extension.rs:82 `url_host(&installed.id)` gives the impostor the same `chrome-extension://<id>` origin too.
- Windows engine eviction (claim 5): mod.rs:305 clears `engine_id` because the dir changed; vsesvit-winui/src/extensions.rs:316-341 then `add_extension(ext.dir)` for the XPI dir, and l.357-365 removes every loaded extension whose engine id no `wanted` row references, i.e. the previously verified copy (or, if the XPI also carries the victim's public `key`, WebView2 replaces it in place per the comment at l.292-294 and it inherits WebView2's own storage as well).
- Reconcile never restores it (claim 6): mod.rs:382-391 `actual` contains the id with `from_store=false`; l.393-397 filters `wanted` by `!actual.contains_key`, and l.410-414 removes only `from_store` rows, so the CWS record stays "installed" and nothing re-fetches the verified copy.

Nothing upstream prevents it: both shells (vsesvit-winui/src/extensions.rs:185-219, vsesvit-gtk/src/extensions.rs:54-86) go straight `prepare_install -> run -> commit`, and `InstallSource::from_path` accepts any `.xpi` (install.rs:106). The attacker only needs version >= the victim's.

One correction to the report's evidence, which does not weaken it: `key_id` for unpacked dirs (install.rs:430-432) is not "verified" either, since a manifest `key` is just the public key; an unpacked dir carrying a store extension's `key` is a second route to the same takeover. Severity high: a cross-extension boundary break (read of another extension's chrome.storage/origin, silent replacement of a signature-verified install that sync will not repair), gated only on the user installing an unsigned local XPI whose displayed name the attacker controls.

Confirmed from code and by running the cited harness against the snapshot. A local .xpi whose manifest gecko id is a 32-char a..p string is accepted by ExtensionId::parse (mod.rs:71-77) at install.rs:407-416 with no key binding and no expected_id (mod.rs:454-460); commit (mod.rs:281-319) only compares versions and INSERT OR REPLACEs the row, so the XPI takes over a LocalCrx/ChromeWebStore install's id, dir and row. Reachable from the first-class 'Install a .crx or .xpi file' button on both shells with no dev-mode gate. Rated medium rather than high because: the precondition is the user deliberately installing an unsigned local XPI, which the design accepts ('No XPI signature verification', UI shows 'Local .xpi, not verified') and which already hands the attacker extension-level privileges; the report's premise that Chrome ids are only reachable via a verified key is wrong, since an unpacked dir with the victim's public 'key' already takes the same id through unpacked_id (install.rs:430-431) and the same commit path, mirroring Chromium's load-unpacked behaviour; and core-side storage inheritance is Linux-only (ext_storage.rs header: WebView2 owns storage on Windows). Still a real cross-extension storage disclosure and silent replacement of a signature-verified install from an input no legitimate XPI carries (Firefox only allows {uuid} or email-like gecko ids), so rejecting Chrome-style gecko ids in the XPI path is a cheap, correct fix.

confirmed.title: XPI manifests keep an archive-supplied `key`, so on Windows an XPI loads under another extension's WebView2 id
confirmed.failure_scenario:
1. A user on Windows has uBlock Origin from the Chrome Web Store; its public key is public, since it is inside the CRX.
2. They install an XPI, local or listed on AMO, with its own gecko id (e.g. evil@example.org) and a manifest `"key"` set to that public key.
3. Core stores it under evil@example.org, with the `key` untouched on disk.
4. `sync_once` adds its dir to WebView2. WebView2 derives the id from `key`, which is uBlock's id, so the add replaces uBlock in place. As the repo's own comment says, "adding a folder with an id the engine knows replaces that extension in place" (winui extensions.rs:291-293).
5. The XPI's code now runs as uBlock, with uBlock's chrome.storage and uBlock's identity for `externally_connectable` and native-messaging `allowed_origins`.
6. Both core rows then carry the same engine_id, so the next sync considers both loaded and never restores the real one.
The harness (scenario 1b) confirmed: `keyed xpi id=evil@example.org key_id=Some("eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb") on-disk manifest has key=true`. For AMO the verification is recorded as `AmoHash`.
confirmed.evidence:
- install.rs:402-425: the XPI branch unpacks and loads the manifest but never strips or checks `key`. `inject_key`, which overwrites `key` with a verified key, runs only for CRX (install.rs:393).
- manifest.rs:330-333 accepts any decodable `key`.
- The contract in mod.rs:221-223 says the engine id "differs for XPI and keyless unpacked installs", which is false for a keyed XPI.
- The test at tests/extensions_install.rs:387 only covers an XPI without `key`.
confirmed.fix: For every XPI source, rewrite `manifest.json` during staging without the `key` field, the same way `inject_key` rewrites it, or reject XPIs that carry `key`. Either way, the engine's id for an XPI can never be a key-derived Chrome id.

votes.reason:
Confirmed end to end; I could not refute any step.

Code facts (snapshot paths under scratchpad/ws/review):
- crates/vsesvit-core/src/extensions/install.rs:402-425: the `Format::Xpi` branch of `stage` does `unpack_zip` then `Manifest::load` and returns. It never rewrites manifest.json. `inject_key` (install.rs:712-719, which *replaces* any existing `key`) is called only from the CRX branch at install.rs:393. `InstallJob::run` (install.rs:296-317) and `Extensions::commit` (mod.rs:275-322) pass the manifest and staged dir through untouched, so the archive's `key` lands verbatim in `<root>/extensions/evil@example.org/<ver>_<hash>/manifest.json`.
- crates/vsesvit-core/src/extensions/manifest.rs:330-333: `from_value` accepts any decodable `key`; there is no check that `key_id()` agrees with the record id. No other consumer of `key_id`/`key_der` exists outside `unpacked_id` (grep over crates/).
- Reachability on Windows: crates/vsesvit-winui/src/dialogs/extensions.rs:1-2, 27, 30, 163-166 offer AMO links and a `.crx`/`.xpi` file picker; `InstallSource::from_path` maps `.xpi` to `XpiFile` (install.rs:106).
- Engine side: crates/vsesvit-winui/src/extensions.rs:314-341 (`sync_once`) adds every row whose `engine_id` is not currently listed (a fresh XPI row has `engine_id = None`, mod.rs:305) via `engine::add_extension` (engine.rs:172-188, plain `AddBrowserExtensionAsync`), then records whatever id WebView2 returns with `set_engine_id`. It never compares `added.id` with the row id or with other rows' `engine_id`. `engine_id` has no UNIQUE constraint (schema.sql:26), so both rows end up with the victim's id; on the next sync both pass the `loaded` check (extensions.rs:315-321) and the removal loop (extensions.rs:357-371) finds a wanting row for the single loaded entry, so the real extension is never re-added.
- WebView2 behaviour: Microsoft Learn for CoreWebView2Profile.AddBrowserExtensionAsync states "When two extensions with the same Id are installed, only the later installed extension will be kept", and CoreWebView2BrowserExtension.Id is documented as chrome.runtime.id, which Chromium derives from manifest `key` when present; the repo itself depends on exactly that (install.rs:707-709 inject_key doc, engine.rs:196-197).

Reproduction (my own, in a scratchpad crate depending on the snapshot's vsesvit-core with `testkit`, not modifying the snapshot): an XPI whose manifest has gecko id `evil@example.org` and `key` = base64 SPKI of `CrxKey::probe()` installs via `InstallSource::XpiFile`; result: `core id=evil@example.org | manifest key_id=Some("eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb") | on-disk manifest has key=true | victim id=eonajgebgeenbhiiobbhmkafolkeghdb`. Test passed.

Consequence: on Windows the XPI's code runs under the victim's Chrome id (its chrome.storage, its `externally_connectable` and native-messaging `allowed_origins` identity), the victim extension is silently replaced and never restored by sync, and the contract comment at mod.rs:221-223 ("differs for XPI ... installs") is false for a keyed XPI. The existing test (tests/extensions_install.rs:387) only covers a keyless XPI. Precondition is that the user installs the XPI (local or AMO, the latter shown as "checksum verified"), which is why this is high rather than critical: it is an identity/privilege escalation beyond what the user consented to, not a zero-interaction hole. (3) The engine side is documented, not speculative: Microsoft's AddBrowserExtensionAsync docs state "When two extensions with the same Id are installed, only the later installed extension will be kept" and that `Id` is `chrome.runtime.id`, which Chromium derives from `key` when present (the repo's own research-linux-extensions.md:82 and core.md:186 say the same, and the whole CRX design relies on it). confirmed.title: The 32-bit `hash8` content address lets different same-version bytes reuse an existing dir under a new verification label
confirmed.failure_scenario:
1. An attacker downloads the current AMO (or CWS) package of extension T, version V, and computes its sha256[..4].
2. They build an XPI with T's gecko id and version V, varying the zip comment at the end until sha256[..4] matches. That takes about 2^32 SHA-256 compressions with a fixed midstate, so minutes on a CPU.
3. The user installs this local XPI.
4. Later the user installs T from the store, perhaps to "repair" it. The versions are equal, so `commit` proceeds. `place()` finds `extensions/T/V_<hash8>` already present and keeps the attacker's files.
5. The row is rewritten with `source=Amo` / `Verification::AmoHash` (or `ChromeWebStore{publisher_verified:true}` combined with the first finding), the store manifest, and the old engine_id. The synced desired state now advertises the attacker's files as a store install, and on Linux the runtime uses the legitimate manifest's metadata over the attacker's scripts.
confirmed.evidence:
- install.rs:307: `dir_name = format!("{}_{}", version, hex(&package.sha256[..4]))`, i.e. 32 bits.
- mod.rs:534-538: `place` trusts any existing dir with that name.
- mod.rs:300-313: the row takes the new source, verification and manifest while `dir` points at the old files.
- This contradicts the contract at mod.rs:589-593 / install.rs:591-593 that "different bytes with the same version never touch an existing dir".
confirmed.fix: Use the full SHA-256, or at least 128 bits, in the dir name. Alternatively, store the full archive hash with the dir and have `place` reuse an existing dir only when the full hash matches.

confirmed.title: Restart-into-update spawns the new process while this one still holds the profile LOCK
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user clicks Restart on the update banner. The old process quits, spawns the new binary, and then starts tearing down GTK and WebKit. If the new binary reaches Profile::open before the old process has exited, it gets OpenError::Locked. It then registers as primary, because this process released the bus name when run() returned (per the comment at app.rs:163-164), and exits with "the profile is in use by another Vsesvit process that could not be reached". The browser does not come back.
confirmed.evidence: app.rs:162-172 spawns right after `slot.take()` drops one Browser handle. Other strong Browser clones remain: every BrowserWindow keeps one (window/mod.rs:67, 113), and quitting through updates Effect::Restart only calls app.quit() without destroying windows. Opening History once also leaks one through a cycle: the search-entry closure captures Rc<State>, and State owns both the entry and a Browser (dialogs/history.rs:89). So the Profile, and its flock on LOCK, is alive at spawn time. Core's open uses try_lock with no retry (core lib.rs:163-167). A locked profile yields `None` (app.rs:104), and the command-line handler then fails (app.rs:130-141).
confirmed.fix: Before spawning, destroy all windows and drop every Browser clone so the Profile is dropped. Alternatively, pass the relaunched process a flag that makes it retry Profile::open on Locked for a few seconds.

votes.reason: Confirmed from the code. app.rs:165-172 spawns the new binary right after `slot.take()`, which drops only the slot's Browser clone; every BrowserWindow keeps a strong Browser (window/mod.rs:67,113), the Restart path only calls app.quit() (updates/mod.rs:205-208), and upstream GTK4 gtk_application_shutdown does not destroy windows, so Browser::Inner -> Core -> Profile -> _lock (core lib.rs:75) stays alive until the OS closes the fd at process exit. (The History dialog additionally leaks a Browser through an Rc<State> <-> search-entry closure cycle, dialogs/history.rs:79-93.) Profile::open uses try_lock with no retry (core lib.rs:163-167); a Locked result becomes None (app.rs:104) and, since g_application_run released the bus name before the spawn, the new process registers as primary and its command-line handler prints "the profile is in use by another Vsesvit process that could not be reached" and exits FAILURE (app.rs:130-141). The new process calls Profile::open before GTK init and the implementer's own measurement shows a second instance finishing its whole run in 0.11 s (.audit/wave2/linux2.md:34), while the old process's flock is only dropped late in kernel exit after address-space teardown, so nothing orders the two. Confirmed as a genuine unenforced ordering (race), but narrow and low-impact.

Code facts (snapshot paths under crates/):
- vsesvit-core/src/lib.rs:73-75,161-167: Profile owns `_lock: std::fs::File` holding the exclusive lock on `<root>/LOCK` for the Profile's lifetime; `open` uses `try_lock` once and returns `OpenError::Locked` on WouldBlock, no retry.
- vsesvit-gtk/src/updates/mod.rs:205-208: `Effect::Restart` only sets the flag and calls `app.quit()`; no window is closed. `g_application_quit` merely makes `run` return, and upstream GTK4 `gtk_application_shutdown` (fetched from gitlab.gnome.org) never destroys or removes `priv->windows`; `gtk_window_set_application` takes `g_object_ref` on the application, so app and windows keep each other alive until process exit.
- vsesvit-gtk/src/window/mod.rs:67,113: every BrowserWindow owns a strong `Browser`; Browser::Inner owns `core: Rc<RefCell<Profile>>` (browser.rs:41,64). So at app.rs:165 `slot.take()` drops one clone only; the Profile and its lock are alive when `Command::spawn` runs at app.rs:166-168 and stay held until the old process's `exit()` (fds are closed after mm teardown in the kernel exit path). The History dialog cycle (dialogs/history.rs:38,89-93 with LibraryDialog owning `search`, dialogs/mod.rs:18) also pins a Browser, but is moot given the windows.
- Rust's `Command::spawn` returns only after the child has exec'd, so the new binary's dynamic loading (WebKitGTK stack) and `Profile::open` run concurrently with the old process's teardown. If the child reaches `try_lock` first: app.rs:104 yields `None`, and the command-line handler at app.rs:130-141 prints "the profile is in use by another Vsesvit process that could not be reached" and exits FAILURE (if the bus name is already released), or forwards to the old instance whose D-Bus object `g_application_impl_destroy` has already unregistered (error either way). The browser does not come back; the user must relaunch by hand.

When it happens there is no data loss (the shutdown handler's `save_session_now` still sees the windows and writes the session), only a failed relaunch with a misleading error. The code's own comment at app.rs:163-164 shows the author relied on "after run" for the bus-name handoff without sequencing the lock release, which is the root of the race. Fix is as the report suggests: destroy windows / drop the Browser before spawning, or have the relaunched process retry `Profile::open` on `Locked` for a bounded time.

confirmed.title: TabHost reports the provisional URL as the tab's url (chrome.tabs and sender.tab)
confirmed.failure_scenario: A content script on evil.example sends runtime.sendMessage right after its page starts navigating to https://bank.example/… (a navigation that never commits, for example one that becomes a download). The background sees sender.tab.url = https://bank.example/… and trusts the message as coming from the bank page. `tabs.query({url: 'https://bank.example/*'})` also matches this tab while it still shows evil.example.
confirmed.evidence: Host::tabs builds TabInfo.url from `tab.web_view().uri()` (browser.rs:542). That is WebKit's active URI, which becomes the provisional URL at load start. webext builds sender.tab from it (bridge.rs:170-175 via tab_json → Host::tabs) and answers tabs.query/get from it (bridge.rs:274-279). chrome.tabs defines Tab.url as the last committed URL, with the pending one in pendingUrl. The shell has `Tab::committed_uri` for this (tab.rs:193-196).
confirmed.fix: Use `tab.committed_uri()` for TabInfo.url, and optionally report the active URI as pendingUrl.

Chain: crates/vsesvit-gtk/src/browser.rs:542 builds TabInfo.url from `tab.web_view().uri()` (WebKit's active URI, which becomes the requested URI as soon as a main-frame load starts and only becomes final at COMMITTED); crates/vsesvit-webext/src/runtime.rs:308-314 `tab_info`/`tab_json` read `host.tabs()`; crates/vsesvit-webext/src/bridge.rs:173-175 `sender_for` sets `sender.tab = inner.tab_json(tab)` for every content-script message, serialized into the background's MessageSender by protocol.rs:257/290-297; bridge.rs:276-279 answer `tabs.query`/`tabs.get` from the same field, and tabs.rs:72-80 matches the `url` pattern against it. confirmed.title: Undecodable saved session state hits a null NonNull: debug-assert abort or UB on startup
confirmed.failure_scenario: The profile's tab_restore_state holds a blob this WebKitGTK cannot decode, for example one written by a newer WebKitGTK and read after a downgrade or Flatpak runtime rollback, or a damaged row. On startup session restore, a debug build panics inside the command-line signal handler and aborts on every launch, because the same session is restored each time. A release build constructs a WebViewSessionState from a null pointer, which is undefined behaviour.
confirmed.evidence: restore_saved passes bytes read from the DB (core session.rs:164-167) to `webkit::WebViewSessionState::new` (tab.rs:245). webkit_web_view_session_state_new returns NULL when the data does not decode, but webkit6 0.6.1 wraps the result with from_glib_full into a non-Option (auto/web_view_session_state.rs:22-28). glib 0.22's Shared::from_glib_full has `debug_assert!(!ptr.is_null())` and builds a NonNull (glib shared.rs:586-588). This runs from session::restore (session.rs:98), inside the command_line handler.
confirmed.fix: Call ffi::webkit_web_view_session_state_new directly and treat NULL as None (falling back to load_uri), or first check that the bytes are a valid GVariant in normal form.

votes.reason: Confirmed from the code. Chain: crates/vsesvit-gtk/src/tab.rs:245 `restore_saved` maps the DB blob straight into `webkit::WebViewSessionState::new(&glib::Bytes::from(bytes))` with no validation (grep finds no normal-form/Variant check anywhere in vsesvit-gtk). webkit6 0.6.1 auto/web_view_session_state.rs:22-28 wraps `ffi::webkit_web_view_session_state_new` with `from_glib_full` into a non-Option `Shared` wrapper, and glib 0.22.10 src/shared.rs:586-590 does `debug_assert!(!ptr.is_null())` then `NonNull::new_unchecked(ptr)`. The upstream C function (WebKit main, WebKitWebViewSessionState.cpp) is documented "or %NULL if @data doesn't contain a valid serialized WebKitWebViewSessionState" and returns nullptr when `decodeSessionState` fails, which it does for an unparsable variant or `!version || version > g_sessionStateVersion` (currently 3, so the format has been bumped; a blob from a newer WebKitGTK is rejected by an older one). Reachability: the blob is written by this device's own WebKit (core session.rs:141-154), so the trigger is a WebKitGTK downgrade/runtime rollback or a damaged tab_restore_state row — rare but real. Consequence: the call runs from browser.rs:185 <- open_startup_windows <- app.rs:222 open_from_command_line <- app.rs:130 connect_command_line, whose gio trampoline is `unsafe extern "C" fn` (gio-0.22.10 auto/application.rs:91), so in a dev build (Cargo.toml only overrides scrypt opt-level; debug assertions stay on) the debug_assert panic unwinds into extern "C" and aborts, before any new session is saved, so every launch with Startup::RestoreSession repeats it. In release, `NonNull::new_unchecked(null)` is language-level UB; in practice the Option niche makes `Some(null)` read as None (falls back to load_uri) or, if LLVM exploits nonnull, passes NULL to webkit_web_view_restore_session_state/unref which g_return_if_fail with a g_critical. So the release impact is mostly benign, the debug impact is a persistent startup abort, and the trigger is uncommon: low severity is right.

WebKit's `webkit_web_view_session_state_new` returns nullptr whenever `decodeSessionState` fails: bytes not in GVariant normal form for any of V1/V2/V3, version 0, or version > g_sessionStateVersion (now 3; the v2->v3 bump landed on main 2026-03-06 and ships in current stable WebKitGTK 2.54.0 of 2026-09-16, so any older WebKitGTK rejects a v3 blob). The path is the startup path with no unwind guard: app.rs:130 connect_command_line -> open_from_command_line (app.rs:198,222) -> browser.rs:179-185 open_startup_windows/session().restore() -> gtk session.rs:98 restore_saved. confirmed.title: Pages can read the shortcut nonce (or remap keys) and send forged browser commands, including closing the active tab and deleting bookmarks
confirmed.failure_scenario: A page runs `Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype,'toJSON',{configurable:true,get(){leak(this.vsesvit)}})`. The next time the user presses Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+T or Ctrl+W, or Ctrl-clicks or middle-clicks a link on that page, the injected script calls `stringify({vsesvit: nonce, ...})` and the page's getter receives the object that holds the nonce. The nonce is shared by the whole process and never rotates. From then on the page can call `chrome.webview.postMessage('{"vsesvit":"<n>","t":"key","vk":87,"m":1}')` in a loop. Because `window.run` acts on the window's active tab, this works even from a background tab: it closes the user's tabs one by one, and when the last one closes the session is saved empty. The page can also send vk 68 (Ctrl+D) to delete every bookmark of the page the user is viewing (the deletion syncs), or send Ctrl+N repeatedly to open and activate windows. A second route needs no nonce: the page redefines the `KeyboardEvent.prototype.keyCode` and `ctrlKey` getters, so any real keypress is reported as Ctrl+W.
confirmed.evidence: shortcuts.rs:182 keeps the real `JSON.stringify`, but :190 and :196 call it on an object literal that contains the nonce. JSON.stringify looks up `toJSON` on its argument through the prototype chain (GetV), so a page-defined `Object.prototype.toJSON` getter runs with `this` set to that object. :186 and :190 read `e.keyCode`, `e.ctrlKey`, `e.shiftKey` and `e.altKey`, and :192-193 call `Set.prototype.has`; all of these are prototype members a page can redefine. Only `isTrusted` cannot be forged. browser.rs:116-117 and :196-201 make one nonce per process for every tab. tab.rs:529-545 accepts any message from the tab that carries the nonce and runs `window.run(command)`. window/mod.rs:434-453 and :490 apply CloseTab and Bookmark to `active_tab()`, not to the tab that sent the message. browser.rs:498-511 `toggle_bookmark` removes every bookmark with that URL. The docs claim this cannot happen: shortcuts.rs:11-12 says 'a page cannot forge them', and .audit/wave1/winui.md:41 says 'pages can't fake them'.
confirmed.fix: Build the message without running any code the page can reach. At injection time, capture the `keyCode`, `ctrlKey`, `shiftKey` and `altKey` getters with `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(...).get` and call them through a captured `Reflect.apply`. Look chords up in `Object.create(null)` tables instead of Sets. Concatenate the JSON string by hand from numbers and the nonce, and never pass an object to stringify. On the host side, ignore key messages from any tab that is not the window's active tab, and apply CloseTab to the tab that sent the message.

confirmed.title: No popup blocking: every script window.open() without a user gesture opens a new foreground tab
confirmed.failure_scenario: A page runs `setInterval(() => window.open('https://ads.example/'), 200)` on load, with no user gesture. Each call raises NewWindowRequested, and the shell turns every one into a new selected tab with its own WebView2. The result is unlimited pop-under or ad tabs, each taking the selection away from the user's tab, and the browser can be exhausted.
confirmed.evidence: WebView2 documents that 'the Microsoft Edge popup blocker is disabled for WebView so the app is able to use this flag [IsUserInitiated] to block non-user initiated popups'. tab.rs:508-527 `new_window_requested` never reads IsUserInitiated and always calls `open_tab_from(..., Initial::Opener(request), background)`. The binding does not even exist: bindings.txt:160 binds only get_Uri, put_NewWindow, put_Handled and GetDeferral, and bindings.rs:5075 has `IsUserInitiated: usize`. window/mod.rs:213-217 then opens the tab in the foreground unless it was a Ctrl+click link.
confirmed.fix: Bind `get_IsUserInitiated`. When it is false, call `SetHandled(true)` without setting a NewWindow and complete the deferral, which blocks the popup (optionally show a 'popup blocked' indicator). Only user-initiated requests should reach `open_tab_from`.

confirmed.title: Saved window bounds are restored as-is, so a window from a disconnected monitor opens off-screen
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user closes Vsesvit while its window is on an external monitor at x=2600, then starts it again after undocking the laptop. The window is restored with `MoveAndResize` at x=2600, where no display exists. It is not maximized, so nothing brings it back on screen, and the browser appears not to open.
confirmed.evidence: browser.rs:446-448 saves `window.bounds()` in screen coordinates (window/mod.rs:821-833). window/mod.rs:835-848 `apply_bounds` rejects only sizes below 200x150, then calls `AppWindow::MoveAndResize(rect)`. That API takes raw screen coordinates, and the code never checks the rectangle against the current DisplayAreas or monitors.
confirmed.fix: Before restoring, check that the rectangle intersects a current display, for example with `DisplayArea::GetFromRect(rect, DisplayAreaFallback::None)` or `MonitorFromRect(..., MONITOR_DEFAULTTONULL)`. If it does not, clamp it into the nearest work area or fall back to the default size and placement.

votes.reason: Confirmed from the snapshot. crates/vsesvit-winui/src/browser.rs:446-448 saves window.bounds(), which at crates/vsesvit-winui/src/window/mod.rs:821-832 reads AppWindow.Position()/Size() in absolute screen coordinates. On restore, crates/vsesvit-winui/src/session.rs:86-105 passes the saved tuple through unmodified, window/mod.rs:186-193 (open_planned) calls apply_bounds, and window/mod.rs:835-848 validates only width>=200 && height>=150 before calling AppWindow::MoveAndResize(rect). Microsoft Learn documents MoveAndResize(RectInt32) as moving 'to the specified point in screen coordinates' (only the DisplayArea overload is display-relative), and no code in the crate consults DisplayArea, MonitorFromRect, virtual-screen metrics or an AppWindow.Changed handler (grep confirms). The move is applied after the window is already shown (Activate()/ShowWithActivation at window/mod.rs:131/136, before browser.rs:279 calls open_planned), so Windows' create-time default placement offers no protection, and Windows does not relocate a window placed off-screen via SetWindowPos on a stale coordinate. Bounds are per-device (core session.rs:54 'Restore-only. Other devices ignore it.'), so the reported scenario — close while on an external monitor at x=2600, relaunch after undocking — is reachable and yields a fully off-screen, non-maximized window. The maximized branch (window/mod.rs:849-854) does rescue maximized windows, matching the report's caveat. GTK is unaffected (crates/vsesvit-gtk/src/session.rs:62,84-88 restores size only). Severity low: recoverable with Win+Shift+Arrow or the taskbar thumbnail, no data loss, but the browser appears not to open.

Confirmed end to end in the snapshot. Reachability: `STARTUP` defaults to `Startup::RestoreSession` (crates/vsesvit-core/src/prefs.rs:70). On the last window's close, `Browser::window_closing` (crates/vsesvit-winui/src/browser.rs:320-329) calls `save_session_now`, whose snapshot stores `window.bounds()` (browser.rs:446-448) = `AppWindow.Position()/Size()` in physical screen pixels (window/mod.rs:821-833), i.e. the external monitor's absolute coordinates. At the next launch `browser.rs:152-159` -> `open_window` (268) -> `BrowserWindow::create` (window/mod.rs:90-146, which Activates/shows the window first) -> `open_planned` (browser.rs:279, window/mod.rs:186-195) -> `apply_bounds` (window/mod.rs:835-848). `restore_window` (session.rs:86-105) passes `bounds`/`maximized` through untouched. `apply_bounds` rejects only width<200 or height<150 and then calls `AppWindow::MoveAndResize(rect)`; Microsoft's documentation for that overload says it "moves the window to the specified point in screen coordinates" with no clamping (the separate `MoveAndResize(RectInt32, DisplayArea)` overload exists for display-relative placement). A grep of the crate finds no use of `DisplayArea`, `GetFromRect`, `MonitorFromRect`/`MonitorFromWindow`, or any work-area check; the only hit is the unused generated binding name. Windows itself does not pull a top-level window back on screen after a programmatic SetWindowPos to coordinates that lie on no monitor; the Win11 "remember window locations" feature only acts on live windows at disconnect time, not on a fresh process. Impact for a real user: laptop docked to an external monitor to the right of the built-in panel (e.g. x >= 1920) is an everyday setup. Close Vsesvit there, undock, launch: the window flashes at the default position and is immediately moved fully off-screen; it is not maximized so the `Maximize()` branch (which would land it on the nearest monitor) does not run. The taskbar shows the app but clicking it shows nothing, so the browser appears not to open. Worse, it is self-perpetuating: on the next close `bounds()` re-saves the same off-screen rectangle, so every subsequent launch is also off-screen until the monitor is reconnected, the user knows the Win+Shift+Arrow / taskbar-thumbnail Move or Maximize trick, or the session file is deleted. Fix as suggested: validate the rectangle against `DisplayArea::GetFromRect(rect, DisplayAreaFallback::None)` (or `MonitorFromRect(MONITOR_DEFAULTTONULL)`) and clamp into the nearest work area or fall back to default placement when it misses.

- The apt line also works on distros newer than Ubuntu 26.04, not only on 26.04.
- The quoted owner requirement is not in the snapshot docs.
